descriptionChirho: Describing something as lasting forever, without end, or belonging to the age to come; modifying nouns such as 'life,' 'fire,' 'punishment,' 'glory,' 'covenant,' and 'Spirit.' The 70 occurrences across all case/gender/number inflections (ANS, AFS, GNS, GFS, NFS, DMP, etc.) represent the same adjectival meaning. Multilingual evidence: Spanish 'eterna/eterno,' Arabic 'abadiyya' (أبدية), Hindi 'anant' (अनन्त), Korean 'yeongwonhan' (영원한), Swahili 'ya milele.'

Used adverbially to mean 'for all eternity' or 'in perpetuity,' functioning as a temporal modifier rather than a nominal modifier. The single occurrence (Rom 1:25 or similar) shifts from attributive adjective to adverbial force. Multilingual evidence shows the shift: Spanish 'eternamente' (adverb, not adjective), Hindi 'sad ke liye' (सद-के-लिये, 'for always'), Korean 'yeongwonhi' (영원히, adverbial -hi suffix), Swahili 'milele' (bare adverb without class prefix 'ya'). This functional distinction warrants a separate sense.
